subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — model routing & policy config
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo notes + integration questions

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency graphs and routing examples were really helpful. A few follow-ups from our engineering and procurement teams: 

- SDK setup and auth: we need guidance for short-lived service account tokens vs API keys (we're AWS-hosted and prefer IAM integrations where possible).
- Model routing/policies: our initial requirement is a latency SLO of 200ms p50 for search assistant queries, but we also need to cap per-token cost for low-priority batch jobs. Curious about how Redwood implements fallback chains (e.g., high-performance model -> quantized cheaper model -> regional fallback).
- Structured output & tool calling: we want to ensure the assistant can call our internal FAQ API and return structured JSON that we can ingest for analytics. Any examples?
- Embeddings/rerankers: are there recommended patterns for hybrid reranking (semantic embedding scores + signals from our internal metadata)?

Can you share an integration checklist and a sample model-routing policy we can review before a follow-up architecture call next week? I'll loop in procurement after we have a rough SLA/quote.

Best,
Liam
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + integration questions

Hi Liam — great to meet you and the team today. Appreciate the clear list. Attaching an integration checklist and a short markdown with model-routing examples to get started (see attachments). A few quick answers inline and proposed next steps below.

Quick answers:
- SDK & auth: Redwood supports API keys and short-lived service tokens; for AWS we offer an optional IAM-backed auth flow for Private deployments and a standard OAuth2 service-account flow for Hosted. We'll send the integration checklist with exact endpoints and token exchange steps.
- Fallback chains: yes — you can define ordered fallback chains by policy. Typical pattern: low-latency variant (fp16) -> quantized 8-bit variant -> low-cost cloud-region fallback. Policies can include predicates (latency budget, cost per-token threshold, model health).
- Structured output/tool calling: we support function/tool calling with schema validation and an enforcement layer that guarantees JSON-shaped responses when configured. I'll include an example tool manifest in the model-routing examples doc.
- Embeddings/rerank: recommended approach is a two-stage pipeline: dense embeddings for candidate retrieval, lightweight model for rerank or a small cross-encoder when latency allows. We can show tradeoffs with cost/latency numbers.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the integration checklist + model-routing examples (attached).
2) Marcus (cc) will follow up with a short proposal for default routing policies tuned to your 200ms p50 SLO and batch cost caps.
3) Can we schedule a 45-min architecture call next Tue (Jun 23) to walk through an initial config and the HubSpot quote? Please confirm availability.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx; model-routing-examples.md

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo notes + integration questions (technical follow-up)

Marissa — looping Dev on some of the deeper integration pieces. Notes for the architecture call and for the draft policy doc: 

1) Auth/SDK: depending on whether Acme wants Hosted vs Private, recommend:
   - Hosted: OAuth2 service account + rotating short-lived tokens (30m) issued by Redwood control plane. Fine-grained scopes for generate/chat/embeddings.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): IAM-backed or mTLS with client certs for zero-trust. We'll include sample Terraform to provision service identities.

2) Routing policy primitives (to capture in the example JSON/YAML policy):
   - matchers: route by request_tag, latency_budget_ms, region, customer_tier
   - actions: select_model, set_quantization_profile, route_region_preference, fallback_chain
   - predicates: token_cost_per_1000 < X, estimated_latency_ms < Y, model_health == healthy

3) Fallback chain example (order matters):
   - primary: try redwood/llama3-70b-fp16 (p50 target 120ms)
   - fallback-1: redwood/llama3-70b-8bit (cost -35%, p50 +40ms)
   - fallback-2: redwood/llama3-13b-region-us-west (regional fallback, cost -60%, p50 +120ms)
   - final: synthetic response generator with cached prefix (for edge cases)

4) Structured output / tool calling: attach a sample tool manifest (name, input_schema, success_criteria). Important: we can enforce strict JSON output and fail open/closed depending on your preference (fail-open returns natural text, fail-closed returns 4xx so your caller can decide).

5) Embeddings + rerank: propose a hybrid scoring function: score = alpha * cosine(embedding_query, doc) + beta * model_rerank_score + gamma * metadata_boost. We'll provide default alpha/beta/gamma and show evaluation on a 1k-query sample.

I'll draft the routing policy template and attach it to the shared drive; Dev, can you add a quick sample YAML with the predicates above?

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + integration questions

Hi Liam — attaching the checklist and the model routing examples we discussed. Summary of recommended defaults for Acme Health to start the POC: 

- Auth: Hosted OAuth2 service account with 30m rotating tokens; we can enable IAM-backed auth if you decide on Private.
- Routing policy (default): p50 latency budget 200ms; primary model: redwood/llama3-70b-fp16; quantized fallback and regional fallback as outlined by Marcus. Auto-escalate to dedicated pool for sustained high throughput.
- Cost control: set token_cost_per_1000 threshold at $0.60 for alerts and $0.80 as hard-cap to trigger regional fallback.
- Structured output: use function schema enforcement (fail-closed) for transactional API calls into Acme systems. We attach a sample tool manifest in model-routing-examples.md.
- Embeddings/rerank: start with Faiss-based candidate retrieval + a lightweight reranker (13B) for sub-200ms p50; move to cross-encoder for high-precision flows where latency permits.

Next steps: 
1) Confirm Tue, Jun 23 at 10:00am PT for a 45-min architecture session (invite to follow).
2) Marcus will push the routing-policy YAML to the shared drive and capture cost/latency estimates.
3) I'll open a HubSpot quote with the SLA proposal (attached redwood-sla-proposal.pdf).

If procurement needs SOC2 evidence, please let me know and I'll loop in our security team — we can share SOC2 Type II evidence and a short security questionnaire.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx; model-routing-examples.md; redwood-sla-proposal.pdf
